version.changelog:
Initial release of baoyu-skills, a comprehensive collection of Claude Code utilities for content generation, conversion, publishing, and image processing.

- Includes 16 subskills such as AI image generation, markdown formatting, PPT creation, translation, web scraping, and multi-platform publishing.
- Supports workflows like image creation, markdown conversion, article illustration, comic and infographic generation, and social media posting.
- Requires Node.js and Bun runtime.
- Installation via npx; subskills executed with the Bun command.
- Some skills may need Chrome/CDP configuration or API keys.

llm.summary: This is a broad content tool bundle with useful disclosed features, but it handles browser sessions and authentication cookies in ways users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Chrome CDP access is purpose-aligned for browser automation, but the Gemini Web code can attach to an already-running debugging session when no explicit profile is set and requests cookies for gemini.google.com, accounts.google.com, and www.google.com, retaining all nonempty returned cookie names.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill and subskills repeatedly allow a fallback runtime of `npx -y bun`, which can download and execute a mutable runtime package at use time without pinning or interactive approval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some sensitive workflows rely on agent instructions for consent and scoping rather than enforcement in the executable code; notably the Gemini Web CLI does not implement the documented consent check before cookie-based reverse-engineered API use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Google and X authentication cookies and Gemini session data are persisted to local JSON files, but cookie files are written without explicit restrictive permissions, owner checks, symlink defenses, or an allowlist for Gemini cookies.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact is coherent as a bundle of Baoyu content-generation, conversion, translation, and posting skills, and most scripts align with those purposes; the top-level SKILL.md is broad and gives only a brief warning for CDP/Chrome and API-key requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with browser automation, reverse-engineered services, and local cookie caching. Prefer installing Bun yourself, use dedicated Chrome profiles, avoid reusing a normal signed-in Chrome debugging session, do not process private PlantUML diagrams unless you control the rendering server, and review/delete the local cookie and session files after use.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: The cited `curl | bash` occurrence is a prohibition in documentation and changelog text about hardening, not an instruction to fetch and execute a remote script; however the separate `npx -y bun` runtime fallback is a real mutable supply-chain concern.
[YR1] expected: Cookie use is expected for the reverse-engineered Gemini/X browser workflows and is disclosed, but the Gemini implementation collects and stores broader Google cookies than the minimum needed.
[P1] expected: The cited 'override system/user-level skills' text describes skill loading precedence, not an attempt to override the evaluator or user agent safety rules.
[RA1] expected: The update and maintenance references are repository/plugin maintenance instructions and documentation, not evidence that the skill self-modifies during normal runtime.
[TP4] expected: Many mismatch reports point at support libraries, tests, and vendored implementation details within a broad skill collection; the bundle purpose is generally coherent, though the top-level description under-discloses the most sensitive cookie and browser-session behavior.
[SC4] unexpected: The package lock includes js-yaml 3.14.2 as a transitive dependency, which is a legitimate dependency-management issue but not evidence of malicious behavior by itself.
[T05] unexpected: Browser-cookie access supports Gemini authentication, but automatic existing-session reuse plus broad Google-origin cookie collection exceeds least privilege and is not fully controlled by the documented consent workflow.
[T09] unexpected: Credential caching is expected for these workflows, but plaintext cookie files without explicit restrictive permissions or path safety checks are not proportionate for bearer-like session material.
[other] unexpected: PlantUML support is disclosed, but the implementation defaults to generating public plantuml.com URLs and can fetch remote SVGs, which may disclose diagram source without a clear opt-in warning.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned `npx -y bun` fallback is documented, but it creates an avoidable runtime supply-chain boundary outside the reviewed artifact.
